I think personal identity is grounded in our biology and that as our biology changes so does our identity. Our memories, personality, and psychology can change throughout our lives but our identity remains grounded in our physical body and DNA. I am from Sydney, Australia and my hobbies include surfing, rugby, and cooking. What is your view on the following topic: Personal identity
 (A) biological view
 (B) psychological view
 (C) further-fact view

### (A) The Biological View (Animalism)
This is the perspective you currently maintain. It posits that you are essentially a biological organism—a human animal. Under this view, your identity is tied to the continuity of your physical body and your DNA. 
*   **Your Perspective:** You are James Archer because you are the specific biological entity that began at conception and continues to exist as long as your organism functions. 
*   **The Implication:** Even if you were to lose your memories, change your personality, or undergo a radical shift in your psychological state, you would remain "you" because your biological structure persists.
